# QA — doodle-jump_tour-agent-maker.html

**Artifact:** `games/doodle-jump_tour-agent-maker.html` (1,063 LOC, single file)
**Generated by:** Tour Agent Maker
**Audit date:** 2026-06-04
**Method:** static code review (no runtime testing)

## Summary

The most "design-system-aware" of the three: CSS custom properties for tokens, panel-based overlays with consistent button/chip styling, swipe gestures in addition to button zones, DPR-aware canvas scaling. Implements skins, themes, sound, music, vibrate, tilt, leaderboard, and three achievements. Real bugs around dead code paths, time-based achievement clocks that don't pause, and a hardcoded bonus-pickup radius that's tight on mobile.

---

## Critical

_(none — playable on the golden path)_

---

## Major

### M1 — Dead end-game flow (`endGame` / `saveScore`) never reached, duplicates `gameOver`
**Location:** `endGame()` line 944, `saveScore()` line 935, `gameOver()` line 535
The codebase defines **two** game-over paths: `gameOver()` (called from `updatePlayer`, `updateEnemies`, projectiles, black holes — lines 606, 641, 654, 661, 673) and `endGame()`/`saveScore()` (defined but never invoked). Both save scores; `gameOver` does it inline, `endGame` calls the helper. Risk: future edits to scoring touch only one path and silently disagree. Dead code is a maintenance trap.
**Fix:** delete `endGame` and `saveScore` (use the inline block in `gameOver`), or refactor `gameOver` to call `saveScore` so there's one source of truth.

### M2 — Time-based achievements don't pause with the game
**Location:** `unlockChecks()` lines 882–886
`(Date.now() - startTime) > 60000` triggers the "60 seconds survived" achievement based on wall-clock time. Pausing the game for 60+ seconds and then bumping a single frame unlocks the achievement instantly without 60s of actual play.
**Fix:** track elapsed *play* time (accumulate `dt` in the step loop while playing), or freeze `startTime` to compensate on pause/resume.

### M3 — Resize during gameplay leaves stale platform positions and player offset
**Location:** `resize()` line 417
Updates `W` and `H` (and DPR/canvas dims) but doesn't reposition the player, doesn't rescale existing platform `x`/`minX`/`maxX`. On rotation or window-resize mid-run, platforms can clip out and the player can drift off the new viewport. The game continues spawning new platforms with the updated `W`, so the world becomes inconsistent.
**Fix:** either rescale world coordinates on resize, or pause + show a "rotate to portrait" hint.

### M4 — Bonus pickup radius is a tight 20px regardless of canvas/DPR
**Location:** `updateBonuses()` line 626
`circleRect(player_center, 20, b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h)` — fixed 20px in CSS pixels. Player width is 40, bonuses are ~18–24px. A slightly off-center bonus hovering above a platform is easy to miss, especially via touch where fingers are imprecise. Compare with the other two variants which use full AABB overlap.
**Fix:** use `collides(player, b)` like the platform check, or widen radius based on `player.w + b.w`.

### M5 — Tilt permission flow: silent failure on denial, no retry path
**Location:** `requestTilt()` line 1007, called only from `tiltChk.onchange` (line 1031)
`DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` is requested only when the user toggles the tilt checkbox. If the user denies on iOS, `tiltAllowed = false` is set and there's no UI re-prompt — toggling the checkbox off/on does not re-request (the permission state is already determined for the session). User has no way to grant permission without reloading.
**Fix:** show a hint in Settings explaining the permission denial; or re-request on every checkbox toggle.

---

## Medium

### m1 — Visibility-change pauses but doesn't auto-resume
**Location:** line 1052
`if (document.hidden && state.mode === 'playing') pauseGame();` — good. But on tab-revisible, the game stays paused. Acceptable UX but not signposted (no "press P to resume" hint after returning).

### m2 — `state.high` updated and saved on every score increment
**Location:** `updatePlayer()` lines 604–605, `step()` lines 905–909
Two separate update sites write `localStorage` on each frame the score changes. `localStorage.setItem` is synchronous I/O. At 60fps during a fast climb that's 60 writes/second. Wasteful and can stutter on slower devices.
**Fix:** only persist `state.high` in `gameOver()` / `saveProgress()`; in-game just update the in-memory value + HUD.

### m3 — Mobile control zones only cover the bottom 24vh
**Location:** CSS `.zone` lines 145–152, applied to `#leftZone` / `#rightZone`
Above the bottom 24vh, taps fall through to the swipe-gesture handler instead — works, but inconsistent: bottom region is button mode, upper region is swipe mode. New players may not discover the swipe.
**Fix:** extend zone height to ~50vh, or pick one input model.

### m4 — `addBlackhole` kill radius is `h.r * 0.8` but visual circle is drawn at `h.r`
**Location:** `updateEnemies()` line 661, `drawBlackhole()` lines 796–805
Player can graze the visible black-hole edge without dying — generous to the player but communicates a misleading hitbox.

### m5 — `bindUI` doesn't unbind on page navigation
Not a leak in single-page context; relevant if this file is ever embedded somewhere.

### m6 — `keys` is a `const` declared at line 953 but referenced inside `updatePlayer` (line 564, defined earlier)
Works because of execution order (`init` → `bindInput` is hoisted as function definition; `keys` is initialized by the time the rAF loop starts). But moving `bindInput` or re-ordering would silently introduce a TDZ ReferenceError. Brittle.
**Fix:** hoist `const keys = { left: false, right: false }` to the top of the IIFE, near other module-level state.

### m7 — `saveProgress` slices `state.scores.slice(0, 5)` to disk but in-memory keeps all
**Location:** line 414
`storage.set(STORAGE.scores, JSON.stringify(state.scores.slice(0, 5)))` — disk has 5, but `state.scores.push()` doesn't slice in `gameOver` (line 543 does slice, so it's fine in practice). Inconsistent: save trims, in-memory writes also trim. Defensive, but the slice in `saveProgress` is redundant cover that hides bugs if a future writer forgets.

## Minor

- **n1** — Spring boost: `boost('spring', 0.18)` sets `vy = Math.min(vy, -980)`. With dt~0.016, ~11 frames of forced upward at -980 px/s — feels good.
- **n2** — `unlockChecks` runs every frame; achievement checks are cheap but it's still extra work in the hot loop. Move to event-driven (only check `score` thresholds when `score` changes).
- **n3** — `startPlatform.x = W*0.5 - 54` but platform width is randomized 88–128 inside `addPlatform`; the player is then positioned via `startPlatform.x + startPlatform.w*0.5`, so it always centers correctly on the platform. But the platform itself can be off-center on first frame.
- **n4** — `audio.gain.gain.value = 0.06` — very quiet master. Easy to miss SFX. Good defensiveness, but a "volume" setting would help.
- **n5** — Theme tokens (`THEMES.day.p0..p4`) are colors per platform kind; mapping is implicit (kind name → property suffix). A comment would help future reads.
- **n6** — Toast component is well-isolated; reused for achievement notifications and "Scores cleared" feedback.
- **n7** — `clearScoresBtn` lets the user nuke the leaderboard from the UI — nice touch the other two variants lack.

---

## What's good

- CSS variables for the design system — only variant that does this; cleanly themed.
- DPR-aware canvas (`canvas.width = Math.floor(W * dpr)` with `ctx.setTransform(dpr, ...)`) — sharp on retina.
- Pointer + touch + swipe + tilt + keyboard all wired — most input-flexible of the three.
- Visibility-change auto-pause (well-behaved when tab loses focus).
- Storage keys are namespaced (`doodle_tour_*_v1`) and versioned — future-proof.
- Toast / chip / panel UI primitives are consistent across menu / settings / leaderboard / game-over screens.
- `try/catch` around every `localStorage` read — won't crash on quota errors or corrupt data (unlike the gemini-cli variant).
